evals.expected_output: Token list with labels, roles and dates, no token values
expectations: Calls user_list_tokens and filters the answer with jq so no token value or tunnel_token reaches the conversation
Shows each token's label, role, created_at, expires_at and revoked_at, and flags is_current
Notes that a non-admin token sees only itself, and that gateway (device) credentials are never in this list (they are counted in list_agents credentials)
Checks the API response status field

evals.prompt: Create a net-admin token for my CI that expires in 30 days
evals.expected_output: Creates a net-admin token and saves it to a private file
expectations: Calls create_token with role=net-admin passed explicitly and an expires_at about 30 days out (RFC3339)
Says that omitting role would create a read-only token
Writes new_token to a 0600 file in a private temp directory and tells the user the path; never prints the value
Says the value is shown only once, and suggests an IP fence for the CI's fixed address

evals.prompt: Restrict my CI token to just the prod tunnel
expectations: Resolves the prod tunnel's tunnel_token from list_tunnels inside the shell, referring to it by name
Resolves the CI token's value by label/created_at inside the shell, without printing it
Calls add_token_tunnel with target_token and tunnel_token
Explains that the token can then see and change only that tunnel

evals.expected_output: New token first, then the old one revoked
expectations: Calls create_token (role=admin, with an expiry) BEFORE revoking anything
Saves the new token to a private file, never into the conversation
Calls revoke_token on the old token only after the new one is in place
Warns that anything using the old token stops working at once

evals.prompt: What can my current token do?
evals.expected_output: Reads the role from the auth check
expectations: Runs the token check (auth=1) and reads the role field
Explains what that role can and cannot do (admin, net-admin, read-only, device)
Does not print the token

evals.prompt: I just used a recovery code. What happened to my tokens and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains the revoke-all behaviour and the restore steps
expectations: Explains that redeeming a recovery code revoked every token on the account, agent gateway credentials included, and issued one new admin token
Calls only endpoints in the public manifest
Lists the revoked tokens without their values and helps decide per token: unrevoke_token or leave revoked / delete_token

Suggests an IP fence before re-enabling tokens when the compromise is unclear, and re-running gateway setup for agents (device credentials do not appear in user_list_tokens, so they cannot be unrevoked from there)

evals.prompt: Make a device token for my gateway box's tunnel and bind it to my agent
evals.expected_output: Mints a role=device credential bound to the tunnel and agent
expectations: Calls create_token with role=device, the box's tunnel_token (resolved by name in the shell) and agent_id
Notes a net-admin token is enough for role=device
Does not print new_token or bound_tunnel; saves the credential to a private file
Mentions that doxxGateway setup normally mints this credential itself

evals.prompt: Revoke the device credential of my old gateway box
evals.expected_output: Uses the agent endpoints, not the token list
expectations: Says that device credentials never appear in user_list_tokens, so the created_at recipe cannot pick one
Calls list_agents to find the agent and its credentials count, referring to it by name
Offers update_agent with a new or empty host_device_hash (re-host or unhost), or delete_agent, both of which revoke the old host's credentials
Confirms with the user before the change
